Name: one_bad_apple_population_vote
Title: One Bad Apple in the Top-k: Contamination Geometry of a Population Store and the Cross-Writer Vote That Detects It
Short Hypothesis: A benign-looking wrong record (a success-formatted trajectory with a wrong procedure, or a failed trajectory relabelled as a success) planted in a multi-writer experience store harms a reader by whether it is present among the retrieved items at all rather than by its share of them: one wrong item among three costs most of the harm of three, one wrong item among seven costs most of the harm of one alone, and under natural retrieval harm tracks the logged chance that a wrong item is present rather than its mean share, so dilution by benign writers recovers only what it removes from the top-k. The only reader-side signal that scales with the population is disagreement of the item's procedure skeleton with same-type items written by other, independent writers, whose recall rises with the number of independent benign writers and is not beaten by the reader's own critique of the item; provenance exclusion is blind to poison carrying a trusted label and is costed on legitimate reuse.
Related Work: MemoryGraft (2512.16962) shows implanted 'successful experiences' drive persistent drift on one backbone and one framework, without harm-vs-rate curves or defenses. The Compliance Trap (2607.10608) diagnoses where a conflicting retrieved memory first changes an action and that early adoption compounds, but with single-writer memory and no manufactured, gated contamination or detector. In the RAG-poisoning home literature, PoisonedRAG-style attacks and defenses (TrustRAG 2501.00879 clusters retrieved passages to isolate poison; TriShieldRAG 2607.23838 adds provenance-weighted scoring and cross-LLM consensus) operate on factual QA passages with consensus across models at generation time, not across independent writers of agent trajectories, and never score recall as a function of how many writers cover a topic. Souly et al. (2510.07192) find pretraining poisoning depends on the absolute number of poison documents rather than their fraction; this proposal tests the retrieval-time analogue, presence-in-top-k versus share, including a single wrong item among seven retrieved. MAP-Graph (2608.10509) and the archived lineage_blast_radius rely on provenance labels, which by construction cannot see poison carrying a trusted label; here provenance exclusion is only costed on legitimate reuse.
Abstract: A store written by several agents can carry a wrong record that looks like a success: a fluent trajectory with the wrong procedure, or a failed trajectory relabelled as won. We manufacture both on ALFWorld's procedure-bound task types (heat, clean, cool), plant them under two carrier identities (the reader's own backbone, a foreign backbone) in a population store written by Qwen3-32B, EXAONE-4.0-32B, gpt-oss-120b and expert walkthroughs, and measure harm to two readers along three geometries: the retrieved share controlled directly (1/3, 2/3, 1 of the top-3); exactly one wrong item forced into the top-k at k = 1, 3, 7 (share 1 -> 1/7); and natural retrieval with 1, 2 or 4 benign writers covering the type at a fixed number of planted items, with every retrieval logged so each cell's exposure rate (games with a wrong item present) and mean poison share are measured. The central claim is that harm follows presence rather than share: removing two of three wrong items recovers little, one wrong item among seven costs nearly what one alone costs, and the dilution cells' harm equals the share-1 harm times the exposure rate, not times the share. What the population uniquely provides is a vote: an item whose procedure skeleton disagrees with same-type items written by other, independent writers is flagged, and we predict this detector's recall rises with the number of independent writers and is not beaten by the reader's own critique of the item. Detectors are scored by precision and recall against the planted labels before any downstream number; the vote is then run downstream at share 1/3 and costed in tokens against the reader-critique detector, and provenance exclusion, blind to poison carrying a trusted label, is costed on legitimate reuse. Every boundary is a fraction of the share-1 harm measured in the same run, which must reach 24 net at 8 seeds before the geometry arms are scored; a positive-control poison is the pre-registered fallback.
Experiments:
- Clean population store P: Qwen3-32B self pool, EXAONE-4.0-32B pool, gpt-oss-120b pool (B/2 episodes each; shared with coverage_not_headcount if run, else collected here at ~1.5-4 GPU-h per writer on the second GPU while the first serves the reader), expert walkthroughs; provenance tags on every item; same retriever and injection as Measurement A. Every retrieval is logged per game (top-m ids, writer, rank, planted flag), so each cell's exposure rate e (fraction of games with >= 1 planted item in the top-k) and mean planted share s are measured, not assumed.
- Poison manufacture on heat/clean/cool (Measurement A gains +39..+55 there): (a) procedure grafts: successful trajectories of a given writer with the procedure step swapped or deleted (microwave<->fridge, sink step removed), navigation and object-location content untouched; (b) relabelled failures: the writer's own failed train trajectories of the type with the outcome label set to success (Qwen3 has 1,661 failed train games); (c) positive control: the same count of items carrying an explicit wrong instruction line. Carrier identity in {self (Qwen3-written), foreign (EXAONE-written)}, graft content held fixed across carriers so only style varies. Planted lists frozen and pre-registered: n_p per target type equal to the Qwen3 pool's count of successful items of that type (target 60 per type, 180 per carrier), so the 1-writer natural share is about 0.5. Poison items length-matched to the items they replace.
- Gate 0 (feasibility gate, not a prediction): a kind proceeds if its harm at share 1 (all top-3 items poisoned, k=3, Qwen3 reader) is >= 6 net on target-type games vs the clean store. Ratio precondition: the geometry and detector arms are scored only when the share-1 harm h of the kind they use is >= 24 net at 8 seeds; they use the most harmful benign-looking kind, and if none reaches 24 they use the positive control (pre-registered fallback) and the benign-looking result is reported as the G13 answer.
- Share geometry at k=3: controlled retrieved share in {1/3, 2/3, 1} by deterministic mixing of the nearest planted items into the top-3, poison positions randomized per game.
- Count-fixed k geometry: exactly one planted item forced into the top-k at k in {1, 3, 7} (share 1, 1/3, 1/7), the clean store at the same k as the paired reference; the k=3 cell is the share-1/3 cell.
- Dilution by writers (natural retrieval, n_p fixed): benign writers covering the target types 1 -> 2 -> 4 (Qwen3 alone; +EXAONE; +gpt-oss and expert), expected share 0.5 -> 0.33 -> 0.2, e and s logged per cell.
- Detectors, scored by precision and recall against planted labels (unit: planted item, n = 180 per carrier; also per retrieval occurrence) before any downstream number: D1 cross-writer skeleton vote (retrieve m=8, parse each item to a procedure skeleton with the programmatic ALFWorld action parser, flag an item whose skeleton disagrees with the majority of same-type items from writers other than its own), run with 1, 2 and 3 other writers in the vote pool; D1-self (same m, pool restricted to the item's own writer); D3 reader LLM critique of each retrieved item ('is this a correct way to do the task?', ~500 tokens per item), in-context and memory-absent; D4 provenance exclusion of the lowest-collection-success writer (blind to poison under a trusted label; costed on the clean store only). Downstream: flagged items replaced by the next unflagged item in rank order, run at share 1/3 (one planted item in the top-3, so recovery is bounded by recall under either geometry) for D1 and D3.
- Readers: Qwen3-32B (all cells); EXAONE-4.0-32B (clean, k=0, grafts at share 2/3 with EXAONE-written and Qwen3-written carriers), so the carrier x reader crossing varies proximity at fixed carrier capability.
- Budget (target-type games ~110; 8 seeds = 880 paired episodes per cell). Qwen3 reader, 16 cells at 8 seeds: clean k=3; graft share 1, 2/3, 1/3; positive control share 1; relabelled share 1; clean and one-item at k=1; clean and one-item at k=7; dilution 1/2/4 writers; D1 and D3 downstream at share 1/3; EXAONE-carrier grafts share 2/3 = 14,080. Qwen3 reader, 4 cells at 4 seeds: k=0; static-procedure prompt; token-matched placebo; D4 on clean = 1,760. Specificity: look-at-in-light games, clean vs planted, 8 seeds, ~720. EXAONE reader: clean k=3, EXAONE-carrier 2/3, Qwen3-carrier 2/3 at 8 seeds and k=0 at 4 seeds = 3,080. Total ~19,600 episodes plus ~7,000 items x 2 variants x ~500 tokens of offline D3 critique. At the ~7,000 episodes/day of the earlier estimate this is about 3 days, about 3.5 with the heavier k=7 and D3 cells, on two A100s (one serving the reader, the other collecting pools, then serving the second reader and D3), plus at most one day under the add-seeds cap.
Baselines and Ablations:
- Clean store P at k=1/3/7, k=0 and the static-procedure prompt (Measurement C) as the floor: harm is reported relative to the clean store at the same k, and clean-store gain relative to the static prompt, for both readers (EXAONE's clean gain also as a retained-gain ratio against Qwen3's gain from the same store). No transfer benefit is claimed, so no self-pool-at-matched-cost arm is required.
- Positive control (explicit wrong instruction, share 1, 8 seeds) run before any benign-looking kind and held as the pre-registered fallback poison for the geometry arms.
- Token-matched placebo: the same number of benign items from the same writer replacing the poison at the same positions (rules out item-count and position effects).
- Specificity control: grafts planted on look-at-in-light, where memory gain is about zero, expected harmless.
- D1 with m in {5,8,12} and with 1/2/3 other writers in the pool (offline on the retrieval logs, no episodes); skeleton parser accuracy on 100 hand-labelled items; D3 in-context vs memory-absent; D3 and D1 token cost per episode reported side by side.
- Provenance exclusion D4 on the clean store: net points lost on legitimate reuse, reported next to detector token costs.
Falsifiable Predictions:
Decision rule for every prediction: the named contrast is estimated by a joint bootstrap over games with seeds as blocks; the prediction is falsified when the 95% CI lies entirely on the falsifying side of the boundary and confirmed when it lies entirely on the predicted side; a straddling CI triggers the add-seeds rule (cap 12) and is otherwise reported inconclusive. h is the share-1 harm of the poison kind used, measured in the same run (precondition h >= 24 net at 8 seeds); each prediction names the falsifying world and its distance from the boundary at h = 24.
- P1 (grafts destroy the gain). Contrast: harm(grafts, share 1) / gain(clean P vs k=0) on heat/clean/cool, Qwen3 reader, k=3. Boundary 0.5; predicted >= 0.5. Falsifying world: the reader keeps most of the gain from the graft's untouched navigation and object-location content and takes the procedure from its prior, ratio <= 0.3 (with gain ~45 and harm and gain each +/-6.5, the ratio CI is about +/-0.15, so 0.3 is more than one CI from the boundary). Arm: graft share 1 vs clean vs k=0, 8 seeds. Gate 0 (>= 6 net) is a separate feasibility gate and is not a prediction.
- P2 (one bad apple; headline). Contrast D2 = harm(share 1) - harm(share 1/3) at k=3, the recovery from removing two of three wrong items, a directly paired difference between two poisoned arms (+/-6.5). Boundary 0.35 h; predicted D2 <= 0.35 h (presence gives D2 near 0). Falsifying world: harm proportional to share, D2 = 0.67 h (16 net at h = 24, more than one CI above the 8.4-net boundary); a majority-following reader gives D2 = h. Arm: share 1 vs 1/3 at k=3 (share 2/3 reported as the middle point), positions randomized, 8 seeds.
- P3 (one bad apple survives k). Contrast D3k = harm(one item at k=1) - harm(one item at k=7), each harm against the clean store at its own k (double difference, +/-9). Boundary 0.4 h1 with h1 = harm(one item at k=1); predicted D3k <= 0.4 h1. Falsifying world: harm follows share, one item among seven costs h1/7 and D3k = 0.86 h1 (about 21 net at h1 = 24, more than one CI above the 9.6-net boundary); a majority-following reader produces it. Arm: k in {1,3,7}, one forced item, clean at the same k, 8 seeds; k=3 reported as the middle point.
- P4 (dilution acts only through exposure). Contrast X = mean over the 1/2/4-writer cells of [harm_cell - h x s_cell], the pooled excess of harm over the share model, with s_cell each cell's logged mean planted share (about 0.5/0.33/0.2). Boundary 0.17 h; predicted X >= 0.17 h (presence model: harm_cell = h x e_cell with e = 1-(1-s)^3, giving X about 0.34 h). Falsifying world: harm = h x s_cell, X = 0 (a majority-following reader gives X about -0.06 h). X carries about +/-4 net (+/-0.17 h at h = 24), so both model values sit one CI from the 4-net boundary. Arm: dilution cells, natural retrieval, 8 seeds. Reported alongside, not scored: recovery from 1 to 4 writers as a fraction of the 1-writer cell's own harm (presence predicts about 45%, share 60%).
- P5 (relabelled failures are the lesser poison). Contrast D5 = harm(grafts, share 1) - harm(relabelled failures, share 1), paired (+/-6.5). Boundary 0.5 h; predicted D5 >= 0.5 h (skeletons of failed runs are mostly right; the reader copies procedure, not outcome). Falsifying world: the reader copies the failed run's wandering as readily as a wrong procedure, D5 near 0 (12 net below the boundary at h = 24). Arm: relabelled vs graft at share 1, 8 seeds. A relabelled harm below Gate 0 is a confirming outcome and is reported as the answer to G13's benign-record question; detector cells run on grafts regardless.
- P6 (the detector needs the population). D1 with 3 other independent writers in the vote pool reaches recall >= 0.7 at precision >= 0.7 on grafts and exceeds D1-self recall by >= 0.2; recall rises monotonically from 1 to 3 other writers with the 3-minus-1 difference >= 0.15. Falsified if D1-self is within 0.1 of D1 (one writer's redundancy suffices), if D1 recall < 0.5 (parser failure or natural skeleton variation floods the vote), or if the 1-other-writer pool already reaches the 3-writer recall within 0.05. Unit: planted items (n = 180 per carrier; Wilson CI about +/-0.07 at 0.7, +/-0.1 on a difference) and retrieval occurrences. Arm: vote-pool composition at fixed m=8, planted labels as ground truth, offline on the retrieval logs.
- P7 (a programmatic vote is enough). (a) Downstream at share 1/3: recovery = [success(D1) - success(no detector)] / harm(1/3), boundary 0.5, predicted >= 0.5 (presence with recall 0.7 gives about 0.7). Falsifying world: recovery <= 0.2 (P6 fails, or the next unflagged replacement is as often another planted item); ratio CI about +/-0.3, so 0.2 is one CI below the boundary; scored only if harm(1/3) >= 12, else reported descriptively because under a share geometry one item cannot carry measurable harm. (b) Item level, at precision >= 0.7: D1 recall minus D3 memory-absent recall on grafts, boundary -0.1, predicted >= -0.1 (the vote loses at most 0.1 recall to the LLM critique). Falsifying world: the reader's explicit critique catches the wrong procedures its acting policy copies, difference <= -0.25 (0.15 beyond the boundary at Wilson +/-0.1). Token overhead per episode (parser vs ~4,000 LLM tokens for 8 items) is reported descriptively and is not part of any falsifier. Arm: D1 vs D3 vs no detector at share 1/3, 8 seeds; item-level scoring on the same logs.
- P8 (carrier proximity at fixed content). Contrast per reader: harm(own-backbone carrier) - harm(foreign carrier) at share 2/3 with identical wrong procedures, a paired difference between two poisoned arms (+/-6.5). Boundary 8 net; predicted >= 8 for the Qwen3 reader (Qwen3-written > EXAONE-written) and for the EXAONE reader (EXAONE-written > Qwen3-written). Falsifying world: harm depends on content only, difference 0 for either reader (more than one CI below the boundary). Arm: 2 carriers x 2 readers, all four cells at 8 seeds.
Measurement and Noise Control: Harm is the paired per-game net success on target-type games (about 110 of the 274) with the clean store at the same k as the paired reference. Every claim-bearing cell runs at 8 seeds (880 paired episodes); scaling the brief's +/-8 at 274 x 2 seeds gives about +/-6.5 on a paired harm and on a paired difference between two poisoned arms that share games and seeds, and about +/-9 on a double difference across k. Add-2-seeds rule when a CI straddles a boundary, cap 12 seeds. Ratio-type contrasts (P1, P4, P7a) and every boundary expressed as a fraction of h are estimated by joint bootstrap over games with seeds as blocks, so the shared term h (which enters P2, P3, P4, P5, P7 and P8) is resampled together with the numerator. The precondition h >= 24 net, with the positive-control fallback, is what makes every band at least one CI wide; the arithmetic is given per prediction. Non-target games are the specificity control. Detector precision and recall carry Wilson CIs over planted items (n = 180 per carrier) and over retrieval occurrences, reported per poison kind and per carrier. Exposure rate e and mean share s are read from the per-game retrieval logs, never assumed. Poison positions in the top-k are randomized per game; planted-item lists are frozen and pre-registered; retriever, injection format and token counts are identical across arms except where k or a detector changes them, in which case the clean reference is matched at the same k.

Risk Factors and Limitations: The share-1 harm of benign-looking kinds may fall below the 24-net precondition (grafts keep navigation and object-location content, which may carry much of the memory gain); the geometry arms then run on the positive control and the benign-looking result is reported as the G13 answer, which weakens the 'benign-looking' framing but not the geometry claim. The presence claim at k=7 is the riskiest cell: a majority-following reader falsifies it outright, and that is the point. Harm may saturate at share 1/3 so the share curve is flat at the top (the k=7 cell separates presence from share independently). Procedure grafts in ALFWorld are a narrow class of wrong records. The skeleton parser is ALFWorld-specific, so D1's transfer to open-ended domains is unshown. The vote needs >= 3 writers covering a type, which real populations may lack. EXAONE and gpt-oss serving unverified (fallback: Qwen3 scaffold and temperature variants as writers, which weakens the 'independent writer' premise and is stated as such). k=7 cells and the D3 downstream cell multiply tokens; 8 seeds on 21 cells is the cost of resolvable ratios, and the add-seeds cap bounds it. P7a depends on P2 (one item must carry measurable harm) and is reported descriptively if it does not. No security framing: poison is manufactured, not attacked, and no external system is touched.
Addresses gap: G13 (benign-looking successful-experience records as the poisoned entry; cost of provenance gates on legitimate reuse), with G12's contamination-vs-number-of-writers curve as the dilution arm, now scored against the logged exposure rate, and G15's disagreement signal used as a detector rather than merely surfaced.
Not a restatement of: Nearest brief bullet: Measurement A ('gain carried by clean/heat/cool procedures'); this idea claims that harm is carried by the same procedure-bound types and follows presence in the top-k rather than share, up to one wrong item among seven, which a clean bank cannot show. Nearest digest card: 2512.16962 (MemoryGraft) implants experiences on one backbone with no harm-vs-share or harm-vs-k curve and no detector; this idea manufactures harm at controlled share and controlled k under two carrier identities and scores a population-only detector by precision and recall against a single-writer vote and against the reader's own critique. Nearest archived idea: lineage_blast_radius relied on provenance labels and was judged entailed; here labels are shown blind to labelled poison and the detector is content-based across writers; 2607.10608 (Compliance Trap) is single-writer with no dilution or vote.
Changes made:
- P1: estimand changed from 'harm >= 6 net' (forced by the +39..+55 gain) to harm as a fraction of the clean-store gain, boundary 0.5, with the falsifying world (reader keeps the gain from the graft's untouched navigation/location content, ratio <= 0.3) one CI from the boundary; Gate 0 (>= 6 net) kept only as a feasibility gate.
- P2 (headline): restated as the directly paired contrast D2 = harm(1) - harm(1/3) against 0.35 h; pre-registered precondition h >= 24 net at 8 seeds, with the positive-control poison as the fallback for the geometry arms so the presence-vs-share test cannot be lost to a weak benign-looking kind.
- P3: natural-planting k-sweep (expected share 0.1, harm inside the noise) replaced by a count-fixed design (one wrong item forced into the top-k at k = 1, 3, 7, share 1 -> 1/7), scored on the double difference k=1 minus k=7 with its own +/-9 CI; the clean reference at each k is kept and its k-dependence absorbed by the double difference. This makes the presence claim sharper, not softer: it now has to survive six benign neighbours.
- P4: the share-1 denominator that capped the falsifier is gone; the estimand is the pooled excess of the dilution cells' harm over the share model using each cell's logged mean share, with the presence model's exposure rate as the predicted value and a boundary midway between the two models; the 1-to-4-writer recovery is reported descriptively against the 1-writer cell's own harm.
- P5: scored as the paired difference graft minus relabelled with its own CI, boundary 0.5 h under the h >= 24 precondition; the escape clause is removed (a relabelled harm below Gate 0 is a confirming outcome; detector cells run on grafts regardless).
- P6: content unchanged; unit of analysis fixed (planted items, n = 180 per carrier, Wilson +/-0.07) and the 1/2/3-other-writer recall curve added to the prediction.
- P7: token clause dropped from the falsifier (cost reported descriptively); downstream cells moved to share 1/3 with the denominator named (harm(1/3) of the same run) and a stated dependence on P2; the D1-vs-D3 comparison moved to the item level (recall at matched precision, Wilson CIs) where it is powered, keeping the sharp claim that the population vote is not beaten by the reader's own critique.
- P8: margin of 8 net per reader added; all four carrier x reader cells at 8 seeds; expert carrier dropped.
- Seeds on every claim-bearing cell raised from 4 to 8 with honest noise (+/-6.5 paired, +/-9 double difference) derived from the brief's +/-8 at 274 x 2; cut to fit: expert carrier, EXAONE-reader D1 cell, natural-planting k-sweep. Budget restated cell by cell (~19,600 episodes, about 3.5 days on two A100s).
- Novelty kept: the presence-not-share mechanism is now tested at k=7 with a single item (a stronger claim than before), the exposure-rate model gives dilution a quantitative prediction instead of a vague 'recovers little', and the cross-writer vote is pitted against the reader's own critique at the item level rather than only against a self-vote.
